first_impression.reaction: Arrived from a Google search for 'wedding ceremony script australia'. Jumped to the FAQ first, as I always do, and it answered the question straight with section numbers. The intro gives the actual legal words and names the Act and the sections in the first two sentences, no fluff about 'your special day'. That's the opposite of what I expected from a wedding company blog, so I kept going. Every legal claim links to legislation.gov.au, AustLII or the Attorney-General's Department and is dated November 2026. I can check all of it myself, which is the point.

journey.quote: In Australia, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say the monitum in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961, which opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect, before you are married.
journey.reaction: Answer first, with the section number. I can verify that in thirty seconds. Good start.

journey.section: What the law requires in an Australian wedding ceremony
journey.quote: General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated and honest about what it is. Repeated a lot down the page, which is a bit much, but I'd rather that than a page pretending to be a lawyer.
Quoted verbatim, attributed, and linked to the source. This is exactly the 'numbers, sources, dates' standard I look for.

journey.section: What the celebrant has to say legally, and what they can change
journey.quote: The Act allows other words that carry the same effect, but how far to depart from the text is your celebrant's judgement, so ask before you change anything.
journey.reaction: Honest about the limits of the page instead of overselling. That's a trade-off stated plainly. More of this, please.

journey.section: Witnesses, the signing and the paperwork on the day
journey.quote: Errors on the certificates can be corrected only while the two of you and your witnesses are still present; once the marriage is registered, only the registry's authorised officer can correct them.
journey.reaction: Practical, specific and the kind of catch I actually want to know about. Useful.

journey.section: The Australian wedding ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=wedding-ceremony-script-australia&utm_content=primary) plans the whole celebration around it.
journey.reaction: First sales line, mid-article. It's after the useful bit so it doesn't bug me much, but 'plans the whole celebration' is vague. Plans what, exactly? Later the page lists venue, travel, vendors and payments. Say that here.

journey.section: Legal wedding vows in Australia and how to add your own
journey.quote: For settings and styling that suit the ceremony you are writing, the [Wedded Wonderland magazine](/magazine?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=lead_magnet&utm_campaign=wedding-ceremony-script-australia&utm_content=magnet) collects ideas from weddings at home and abroad.
journey.reaction: Not for me. Styling ideas in the middle of a legal section. I skipped it. Harmless, but it's filler.

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the first brand line I'd actually screenshot. But it tells me when the fee is agreed, not how it's structured or whether you also take a cut from the suppliers. And 'payments' makes me ask: do supplier payments flow through you, and is there a margin on them?

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: Speak with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=wedding-ceremony-script-australia&utm_content=secondary) about the celebration that follows the legal one.
journey.reaction: Wedded Advisor, then Wedded Concierge in the next sentence. Is Concierge a person, a service tier, a different product with its own fee? Two brand names for what reads like the same thing makes me wonder what I'm being moved into.

journey.section: Plan the day around the words
journey.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Concrete process claims, no 'best' or 'award-winning'. I respect that. Still doesn't answer the commission question, which is the one I'd lead with on a call.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor fee structured (flat, percentage, tiered)? The page says it is agreed in writing, not what it is based on.
Do you take a commission or referral fee from venues or suppliers, and are supplier prices passed through at cost?
When the Advisor handles 'payments', do supplier payments go through Wedded Wonderland, and is anything added on top?
What is the difference between Wedded Concierge and a Wedded Advisor? Is Concierge a separate service with its own fee?
Is there a real wedding I can look at with the actual budget breakdown?

turn_offs_found.quote: [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=wedding-ceremony-script-australia&utm_content=primary) plans the whole celebration around it.
turn_offs_found.why: Vague promise. 'The whole celebration' says nothing about what the fee buys. Minor, because it sits after a lot of genuinely useful content.

would_share_with: My partner, for the script itself
A mate getting married in Australia who asked what the celebrant legally has to say

cta_reaction.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The article earned some credibility: it's sourced, dated and doesn't oversell. The written quote and written inclusions lines are the right signals. But I'm comparing three planners and the page doesn't tell me how the fee works or whether you take a cut from suppliers, so I'd go to the services or FAQ page before I'd enquire. I wouldn't click from this post alone unless the next page answers that.

top_3_changes: Make the first CTA concrete using only the services the page already names later. OLD: "plans the whole celebration around it." NEW: "can plan the venue, travel, vendors and payments around it."

Make the Concierge and Advisor relationship clear in the overseas section, consistent with the closing paragraph. OLD: "Speak with [Wedded Concierge](" NEW: "Speak with a Wedded Advisor through [Wedded Concierge]("

Do not add fee or commission detail to this post without brand sign-off, but make sure the /wonderland-concierge destination answers 'how is the fee structured' and 'do you take a cut from suppliers' up front. That is what decides whether a sceptic enquires after this article (see open question to orchestrator).
